Agha hit 107 off 90 balls and Pakistan scored 305 all out in 49.5 overs after Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis won his fourth successive toss and chose to field.

Captain Shaheen Afridi picked up 3-55 while Naseem Shah pinned down Sri Lanka's top-order with impressive swing bowling to finish with 2-43. Haris Rauf ran through the tail with 2-48 while seam all-rounder Faheem Ashraf grabbed 2-49, including the key wicket of Rathnayake.

The injury is also a blow for PSG coach Luis Enrique, given that Mendes would likely have marked Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal in their Champions League game on Tuesday.
Yamal operates from the right flank and often cuts inside. The 19-year-old Yamal has scored nine goals overall this season for Barcelona, which has won all its 11 games so far in La Liga and Champions League, and has also been in terrific form for Spain.

articles.title: Fire at Canada military base kills 4
articles.summary: Alberta: Four Canadian service members were killed and 39 people injured, including 19 critically, when a fast-moving fire overtook soldiers conducting live-fire combat training at a military base in Alberta, officials said Sunday.Maj. Gen. Wade Rutland said military officials knew about the fire for hours but believed it was sufficiently contained to allow training to continue before winds suddenly shifted, sending flames racing toward the soldiers."The fire was a kilometer away when the wind shifted. That is not normal for a fire to move a kilometer in 36 seconds," he said at a news conference in Edmonton.Rutland said a commander at the scene told him soldiers went from seeing no fire to having flames upon them in less than a minute.The fire broke out Saturday during high-intensity combat training involving Charlie Company of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry.About 84 soldiers were split between a grenade range and an area where they practiced attacks on simulated enemy positions. The fire swept into the second training area.Rutland said investigators had not determined what ignited the grass fire.He said the battalion was preparing for rapid deployment to global crises and a mission to reinforce Canadian troops in Latvia next spring.The military identified those killed as Sgt. Morgan Wong of the Loyal Edmonton Regiment and Privates Shaun Farrell, Aidan Goulding and Hayden Lykkemark of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry. All four were serving with the battalion, based in Edmonton.Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said 39 people were receiving medical care. Sayeh Zielke, chief executive of Acute Care Alberta, said 19 were in critical condition, eight were stable and 12 were ambulatory and receiving treatment for less serious injuries.Smith said some suffered severe burns and could face weeks or months of intensive treatment.Prime Minister Mark Carney described the incident as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on domestic soil. He ordered flags lowered to half-staff on federal buildings nationwide.Carney said the families of those killed had been notified. Those affected included regular forces personnel, reservists and soldiers from bases across Canada.Hospitals respond to mass casualtiesAlberta health officials said patients were transferred from Wainwright to four hospitals - the University of Alberta Hospital and Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton, Foothills Medical Centre in Calgary and Red Deer Regional Hospital.Alberta officials said they had lifted the "Code Orange" emergency activated at several hospitals Saturday night to mobilize staff and beds for the casualties.The response involved 22 ground ambulances, six airplanes and two helicopters, with assistance from neighboring Saskatchewan. Smith said all patients had been accounted for and no further patients were awaiting transport.Wainwright Mayor Bruce Pugh said the town's small hospital was not designed to handle a mass-casualty incident but praised local medical personnel.Rutland confirmed that military search-and-rescue technicians parachuted into Wainwright to reinforce the emergency response. Pugh said their red parachutes were illuminated by flares as they descended shortly before midnight.Cathy Keane, a mayoral candidate in Ontario, said her eldest son was among those critically injured. "As a mother, right now I need to be with my son and family," she wrote on Facebook, saying she was traveling to Alberta.Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre, who represents the area in Parliament, visited Wainwright on Sunday and said he had heard accounts of people who ran toward the danger to help others and were now fighting for their lives in hospitals.Military invest igates fireRutland said the fire ignited in the military training area, where multiple exercises were underway, and spread rapidly in unusually strong winds.He said winds had been within normal operating limits for much of Saturday, generally below 50 kph (31 mph), before intensifying rapidly. Range controllers rely on weather reports to determine whether training can safely continue, he said.The fire crossed established firebreaks before being contained with help from municipal firefighters.The Canadian military said there were no indications of terrorism.Rutland said military investigators would examine the circumstances, including whether safety protocols needed to change. "If our protocols need to change, then they'll be updated," he said.The military typically convenes a formal board of inquiry after such incidents, Rutland said, cautioning that determining what happened would take time.Rutland said Charlie Company had been withdrawn from the training area and the rest of the battalion suspended training Sunday.The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said officers were called shortly after 4 p.m. Saturday following reports of a fire in the base's training area.Large areas of Alberta were hit by a windstorm Saturday, with gusts up to 100 kph (62 mph). The winds toppled trees, sent signs flying and pushed flames beyond the base into surrounding rural areas.By late Saturday, the Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire was being held and that property and critical infrastructure were protected. No evacuation order was issued for residents.CFB Wainwright is one of Canada's busiest military training bases, where soldiers prepare for combat operations.The fire also disrupted advance voting ahead of Monday's referendum on whether Alberta should begin a process that could lead to independence from Canada. Elections Alberta said the Wainwright Communiplex advance polling location closed early Saturday and election materials were transported securely.

articles.title: Ukraine fires over 1000 drones at Russia
articles.summary: Ukrainian strikes set an oil export terminal and a depot ablaze in St. Petersburg on Sunday as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war.The strikes came as tensions between Kyiv and Washington deepened, with U.S. President Donald Trump criticizing Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure and the prospect of further U.S. sanctions against Moscow still uncertain.Also read: Trump claims 'great progress' in Russia-Ukraine negotiations; accuses Zelenskyy of not making better deal 2 years agoTrump said Sunday that he decided to hold off on implementing new sanctions on Russia because he doesn't "want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table."In a social media post, the U.S. president defended his Friday order to issue a waiver to prevent new sanctions from being placed on Moscow from bipartisan criticism that he was favoring Russian President Vladimir Putin's interests over those of Ukraine. Trump said he believed new sanctions would undermine negotiations to bring about a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine."I can sign it later, or any time that I want!" Trump added of the sanctions.Trump also lashed out at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has been critical of Trump's recent outreach to Putin, for launching strikes on Russian energy infrastructure during the conflict, claiming Zelenskyy "doesn't want to end this war."Zelenskyy: Waiving sanctions strengthens RussiaSpeaking on NBC's "Meet the Press" earlier on Sunday, Zelenskyy said waiving sanctions against Russia would strengthen Putin's war effort. He also said U.S.-Ukraine intelligence sharing had resumed after being "blocked for some period of time."Zelenskyy said that while he trusted Trump, siding with Moscow would be a tragedy and a "historic mistake" for Washington."People want to forget what's going on. But we can't give this possibility to forget, or to change reality, or to change the truth," Zelenskyy said. "We can't compare me and Putin. He's (an) aggressor. He occupied us. He killed adults and children, his soldiers. He's a terrorist. And that's why I hope that President Trump will be very clear with this position."Later Sunday, Zelenskyy said on social media that he had spoken with U.S. presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about the results of an Oct. 9 meeting between U.S. and Ukrainian negotiating teams in Miami, as well as "next steps in diplomacy."Two killed as Russia and Ukraine trade blowsOne person was killed and five others were wounded in the St. Petersburg attack, which sparked fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city's Ruchi oil depot, local Gov. Alexander Beglov said. A logistics center belonging to Russian retailer Ozon and a data center operated by Russian tech giant VK were also targeted, the companies confirmed.Russia's Defense Ministry said Sunday that its forces had destroyed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions, the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea.Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russian state news agency Tass that Kyiv was "resisting" Moscow's invasion but could not "change the current course of events."Meanwhile, in Ukraine, a woman was killed and a 6-year-old girl was among at least two other people wounded in two Russian attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, local officials said Sunday.Russia continues energy attacks, Kyiv saysTrump announced on Oct. 11 that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire" in the 4½-year-old war, but offered no details. Kyiv reported Russian attacks on energy sites continued after Trump's announcement, and on Thursday said it had resumed strikes on Russian oil facilities after a three-day pause.Zelenskyy wrote on X on Sunday that Russia had attacked Ukraine's energy, oil and gas sectors 76 times in the week since Trump's announcement. The Ukrainian government initially said it was observing the ceasefire.Also read: Trump's decision to waive Russian sanctions outrages Congress, but no quick counter seenEnergy facilities in four Ukrainian regions were struck overnight, leaving tens of thousands of families without power, he said, accusing Russia of trying to cause a blackout."America should see that Russia is not taking any reciprocal steps in response to sanctions relief or agreements. On the contrary, they take every signal of an opportunity to make money as proof that their bet on war is paying off and they can keep fighting," the Ukrainian president wrote.Ukraine apology to Lithuania over drone alertUkraine's Foreign Ministry apologized on Sunday after a drone entered Lithuania's airspace, prompting authorities to issue an air raid warning.Russian electronic warfare may have diverted the drone during a Ukrainian operation against legitimate military targets in Russia, ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi said in a statement.Lithuanian authorities urged residents in two northern counties along the Latvian border to take cover early Sunday because of a possible drone incursion, public broadcaster LRT reported.A drone entered the northern Pasvalys region and damaged a moving car, LRT said, citing Lithuania's National Crisis Management Center. No injuries were reported.

The value had reached a record ₹4.03 lakh crore in November 2025.Infosys, which was among the five largest holdings of mutual funds at the start of 2026, slipped to 10th place in September. TCS has seen a similar decline. The stock, which ranked 10th among mutual fund holdings in 2024 and was among the top 14 in 2025, slipped to 18th place in September.HCL Tech and Tech Mahindra, which ranked 20th and 25th among mutual funds' largest holdings at the beginning of 2026, slipped to 25th and 31st positions, respectively, in September. Exporters may have to track emissions
articles.summary: New Delhi: The government has begun discussions on whether Indian exporters should track indirect emissions across their supply chains as trade partners tighten green requirements and global value chains become increasingly interconnected.The finance and commerce & industry ministries have held preliminary discussions on whether Scope 3 emissions should be measured for exports to all countries, rather than only for markets such as the European Union and the UK, which have introduced Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) measures.Scope 3 emissions cover indirect emissions across a company's value chain, including those linked to purchased goods and services, capital goods, transportation, waste, business travel, employee commuting, leased assets, raw material extraction and the sourcing of imported raw materials. Measuring them is more complex than tracking emissions directly generated by a company or those associated with the energy it purchases.Also Read | Faster services imports threaten to erode cushion against India’s goods trade deficit: Report"There is one thought that measurement of Scope 3 emissions can't be done for the EU alone. It would have to do for all countries because the value chains are linked," said an official, adding that the indirect nature of these emissions makes them particularly challenging to measure, report and mitigate. However, no decision has been taken on the issue.Niti Aayog, in its report titled Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat And Net Zero: Financing Needs, has said that any inclusion of Scope 3 disclosures should be phased and proportionate, beginning with large entities in high-impact sectors to avoid imposing disproportionate compliance burdens on micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and smaller suppliers.135034854The existing CBAM frameworks provide for the determination of direct and indirect greenhouse gas emissions covered under Scopes 1 and 2 of the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. Indian exporters of iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen products are already subject to the EU's CBAM.Also Read | What is holding up the US-India trade deal?"The CBAM is already a challenge for us because we don't have basic data on our raw material emissions. Disclosures on Scope 2 are posing a problem, so adding Scope 3 emissions data on what is my electricity provider and transportation would be unviable," said a steel exporter to the EU. Under the EU CBAM, the central platform will open for the sale of CBAM certificates on February 1, 2027. Importers must submit their first annual CBAM declaration and surrender certificates covering all 2026 imports by September 30, 2027.

articles.title: Europe refused China, India oil sanctions
articles.summary: Washington, Amid intense criticism, the US on Sunday said the waiver of sanctions on Russia and tariffs on other countries, including India, was a 60-day pause to analyse the global impact of the measure.Trump's cabinet colleagues Marco Rubio and Scott Bessent said the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act granted the President the flexibility to assess the situation."No sanctions were lifted on Friday," Bessent told NBC's Meet the Press, referring to the Executive Order signed by Trump granting a waiver from sanctions under the Graham Act passed with overwhelming bipartisan support last month.Bessent revealed that the US had asked its European allies to impose secondary sanctions on China and India for buying Russian oil, but they refused."So why should the US bear the burden? President Trump, perhaps we will be in contact with our European partners. Why should the US go it alone," Bessent said, adding that European countries had waived an embargo on purchase of Russian diesel and jet fuel in May.On Saturday evening, Secretary of State Rubio said waivers were included in the Graham Act to study the different things going around the world, such as the pressure on global energy supplies due to the Iran war, the attack of Houthis in Saudi Arabia and the Ukraine-Russia war."I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy, and even to the US economy," Rubio told reporters before leaving on a six-day visit to Uzbekistan and India.The executive order signed by Trump on Friday states that the waivers shall remain in effect until such time as the President or the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Trade Representative, as appropriate, determine that further action is appropriate.Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago resort near Miami on Saturday, Trump said his decision to waive sanctions under the Graham Act would benefit the US."A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out,"  he said."It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world because we're really at a world stage,"  Trump said.Bessent also accused the European nations of fuelling Russia's war on Ukraine by buying oil and gas from Moscow."The Europeans have given Russia and Vladimir Putin more money than they've given the Ukrainians. They continue to gorge on Russian energy," Bessent said."The Europeans are financing the Russian war machine. The US imports USD four billion of Russian products. USD 1.8 billion of that is fertiliser. The Europeans import more than 10 times that," Bessent said.Trump's decision to waive sanctions on Russia came under fire from the Republicans and Democrats, who last month came together to overwhelmingly pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.Senator Darline Graham, a Republican from South Carolina, also criticised Trump for exempting Russia from a sanctions law that was championed by and named after her late brother Lindsey.Indian-American lawmakers, most of whom had voted against the Graham Act, were sharply critical of Trump's decision."Trump's decision to waive new sanctions on Russia should leave no doubt: that is exactly what is happening," Congressman Ami Bera said on X."My Republican colleagues pushed hard to pass the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions bill before we left town. They ought to be standing up and screaming at the top of their lungs that we don't side with Russia," he said."Trump is doing exactly what we warned: undermining Congress' authority, abandoning Ukraine, and letting Putin off the hook," Congressman Suhas Subramanyam said on X."Republicans refused to let us vote on stronger Russia sanctions. Now we - and our allies - are paying the price," Subramanyam said.

articles.summary: In a historic step, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) will implement a major functional reorganisation of its administrative and operational structure from November 1 to strengthen specialised security management across critical infrastructure and strategic establishments nationwide.The reorganisation, approved by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), will realign the force's existing territorial sectors according to the specific security requirements of different industries and establishments, including power, coal, steel, petroleum and natural gas, ports, government buildings, museums, monuments and mass rapid transit systems.Under the revised structure, the force said, the National Capital Region Sector will be reorganised as the Government Building Museums and Monuments and Mass Rapid Transit System (GBMM & MRTS) Sector, New Delhi.The North Sector in New Delhi and North Eastern Sector-II in Kolkata will be restructured as the Power-I and Power-II Sectors, respectively. The Eastern Sector in Ranchi will become the Coal Sector, while the Central Sector in Bhilai will be converted into the Steel Sector.Similarly, the North Eastern Sector in Guwahati will become the Petroleum and Natural Gas Sector. The Western Sector in Mumbai and the South Sector in Chennai will be transformed into the West Coast Port Sector and East Coast Port Sector, respectively.The existing Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space (DAE & DoS) Sector in Bengaluru, Airport Sector-I in New Delhi and Airport Sector-II in Bengaluru will continue under their respective functional arrangements.The reorganisation, it said, aims to improve operational oversight, develop sector-specific expertise, ensure greater uniformity in security practices and strengthen coordination with the concerned ministries, departments and installation managements.The CISF provides security to a wide range of establishments, including airports, seaports, atomic energy and space installations, power plants, power grids, steel plants, coal mines, petroleum and natural gas facilities, currency note presses, government buildings, iconic monuments and mass transit systems.Each sector has distinct operational processes, infrastructure, potential hazards and security vulnerabilities, requiring specialised security arrangements.Under the earlier system, administrative and operational supervision was largely organised on the basis of territorial jurisdiction. Over the past 25 years, the force has progressively adopted a functional approach in selected sectors, including aviation and strategic establishments under the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Space.The experience gained from this approach highlighted the advantages of specialised supervision, focused training, sector-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), better utilisation of specialised personnel and closer coordination with the concerned organisations.Building on this experience, the CISF reviewed the supervisory structure of the remaining territorial sectors and undertook the functional realignment following deliberations with supervisory formations, branches at force headquarters and senior officers, before obtaining MHA approval.The restructuring assumes significance as the CISF's mandate is expanding beyond conventional industrial security to cover new and specialised responsibilities.The force has been designated as a Recognised Security Organisation (RSO) for port facilities under the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code. The functional realignment of port-sector supervision is expected to support specialised port-security expertise and improve coordination with port authorities and other stakeholders.The CISF has also been entrusted with security responsibilities at high-security correctional facilities in Jammu and Kashmir and designated as the nodal agency for aerial security of critical infrastructure.The force is strengthening its cybersecurity and drone and anti-drone capabilities through specialised training and collaboration with premier institutions to improve preparedness against cyberattacks, digital threats and hostile unmanned aerial systems.The reorganisation is expected to establish a more specialised, sector-oriented security apparatus, improve operational accountability and strengthen protection of India's strategic and economic assets.

articles.title: Trivandrum airport halts flights on Tue
articles.summary: Flight operations at Thiruvananthapuram International Airport will be suspended for five hours on October 20 to allow the traditional Arattu procession of Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple to pass across the runway.Thiruvananthapuram International Airport Ltd (TIAL) said on Sunday that flight services would remain suspended from 4 pm to 9 pm to facilitate the temple’s ‘Alpassi Arattu’ procession. The runway crossing is a distinctive feature of the ceremony, reflecting the historical relationship between the temple, the former royal family and the airport. The temporary closure requires airlines to adjust their schedules to accommodate the procession.Passengers travelling to or from Thiruvananthapuram on October 20 should check with their airlines for updated departure and arrival times before heading to the airport.
